children: Japan's Nikkei share average fell more than 3% on Wednesday, dragged down by sharp drops for AI-related stocks, though the overall decline was limited as investors scooped up defensive stocks.
fell 3.3% to 56,710.43 by the midday break, while the broader Topix
was down 1% at 3,727.24.    Wall Street retreated on Tuesday, with tech stocks giving back some of the Monday rally sparked by Jensen Huang's surprise return to Nvidia
"It was hard to buy AI-related stocks after overnight declines of technology stocks on Wall Street," said Takamasa Ikeda, senior portfolio manager at GCI Asset Management.
"But investors bought other stocks that failed to ride on a rally in the previous session," he said.
Among the biggest decliners on Wednesday were Advantest
and chip-making equipment maker Tokyo Electron
But drugmakers rose, with Otsuka Holdings
jumping more than 6% each to become the top percentage gainers on the Nikkei.

Of more than 1,500 stocks trading on the Tokyo Stock Exchange's prime market, 56% rose, 41% fell and 2% traded flat.
